_readme: Committed p95 latency budgets for the nightly-load-test CI job (#1082). See docs/development/nightly-load-test.md for the full contract: fixture size, budget-derivation rule, and how to re-derive this file at each release. DO NOT hand-edit budget_p95_ms to a round number — every value here must trace to a measured_p95_ms via the stated formula.
status_note: Re-derived 2026-11-19 (#2110, #2237, #2063) from job 18170442650 -- the 2026-11-19 scheduled nightly-load-test run on main at f863f39ff on gitlab-runner-nuc-2-visiban (tag nuc). Values below are that run's measured p95/p99 per endpoint, unchanged from the artifact, with budget_p95_ms recomputed via the formula for the whole file in one pass; the ten flow/summary/analytics scenarios (#2110) and card_list/cards_archived (#2237) get their first budgets and their pending_budget keys are gone. card_timeline_counts (#2195) and the three board_movements scenarios (#2237) were added after that run, so they are measured but not gated (pending_budget) until a NUC run that includes them re-derives the whole file again. This is a single run: board_full measured 824.5ms against 1227.5ms in the previous derivation, so its budget fell from 1720 to 1155ms; the two derivations were taken on the same runner class but a different commit and a different date, so the change is not attributed here. Peak memory (#2110, #2430): the script records the server's peak RSS per scenario when given --server-pid-file; every memory budget is pending (budget_peak_rss_mb null, pending_memory_budget) until a NUC run assigns it. History: 2026-10-21 (#1808) from job 17348200339 on gitlab-runner-nuc-2-visiban; 2026-10-20 (#1767) from job 17304593759 on runner-04-NUC; 2026-09-30 (#1233) from job 16796708105. Re-derive again at the next release per docs/development/nightly-load-test.md#re-deriving-the-baseline. #2430/#2424 added the aged-board, linked-board and overview fan-out scenarios; they have no measurement yet, so they are all pending_budget against #2430 until that NUC run.

fixture.note: --scale 20 replicates the 10-swimlane demo layout 20x (11-13 cards/swimlane, same distribution as the normal demo board) rather than picking an arbitrary target card count directly. The load-test board has 20 members (5 demo users + 15 loadtest* filler accounts, #1723).
fixture.multi_board_note: #1810: --extra-boards 199 adds 199 small boards (8 cards each, 1,592 cards) owned by demo3, so demo3 can access 200 boards with the load-test board. The extra boards belong to demo3 alone, so the demo1 board_list and demo2 scenarios see the same boards as before. Every measured_p95_ms in this file was taken with the extra boards present (#1808).
fixture.aged_and_linked: #2430/#2424: seed_demo_data also gets --aged-generations N and --linked-boards. Both fixtures live on boards only the loadtest_analytics user can open, so what viewers can see is unchanged. Row counts grow (cards about 4k to about 16.5k, movements about 5x, with the aged fixture on), so the existing budgets may move: expected, not proven (as #1810). The isolation is about board access, not authorship (demo1-5 still author and are assigned the aged cards). Known limit: aged copies carry movements only, no CardBlock history, and blocked_at/due_date are not shifted, so aged_flow_blocked is not an aged-history measurement.

measurement_method.percentile_method: nearest-rank (no interpolation) over the 40 timed samples
measurement_method.auth: manage.py provision_fuzz_token --username demo2 (scoped, non-admin PAT; board_list alone authenticates as the board owner demo1 via --owner-token-file — same mechanism backend-schema-fuzz already uses)

budget_formula: budget_p95_ms = ceil(measured_p95_ms * 1.4 / 5) * 5 -- a 1.4x factor (issue #1082 specifies 1.3-1.5x) rounded up to the nearest 5ms so CI comparisons have a little headroom for measurement noise without the number itself being picked round. Recompute this whole file -- never hand-adjust a single budget_p95_ms -- when re-deriving.

board_list.note: Board list as the board OWNER (demo1, via --owner-token-file) so the access query spans the 20-member board; member_count/card_count/archived_card_count are independent correlated subqueries (#1723).

board_full.note: Serializes the entire board (all 2388 cards) in one response, unpaginated -- the most volume-sensitive endpoint in the fixture and the one this budget is least tolerant of relative headroom on, since a regression here is the one TruePPM's #2767 postmortem describes (index-shape regression, identical query count, higher latency). Also the most CPU-bound of the six (per-card DRF field serialization across ~2,388 cards, #1212), so it shows the most run-to-run variance on a shared CI runner -- expect wider swings here than on the lighter endpoints below.

card_search.note: The cross-board card query as a one-board user (demo2): access filter plus one 51-row cursor page. Card search now filters with the ci_contains lookup (ILIKE on PostgreSQL), which the pg_trgm GIN indexes from migration 0030 (card_title_trgm_idx / card_desc_trgm_idx) can serve for selective terms (#1809). The budget was re-derived from NUC job 18170442650 and broad/short terms re-measured in #2063 (plans in docs/development/nightly-load-test.md). Derived after the #1805 fix (#1808). 'the' is a deliberately broad, high-cardinality search term -- it matches a large fraction of the corpus, closer to a real user's search-as-you-type behavior than a highly selective term would be.

card_search_multi_board.note: The same query as card_search, run as demo3, who can access 200 boards, so the card SELECT filters on a 200-id literal list. PostgreSQL is expected to scan the matching cards and sort instead of walking card_board_updated_idx (#1805 measured 13.5ms vs 0.65ms execution on the one-board fixture; this fixture layout was not EXPLAINed, so the plan is expected, not confirmed). Budget derived from a NUC run in #1808.

card_timeline.note: Unified movement + activity feed for a single card. Exercises the comment_card_created_idx / activity_card_created_idx composite indexes added in migration 0045. NOTE (#2365): the timeline now also returns gate entries, but the fixture seeds no gate rows, so the p95 here does not yet measure gate work; re-derive this budget with gate rows seeded.

card_timeline_counts.note: The card detail sheet's request (#967): the timeline page plus the per-group counts queries, on every card open and every card.version change. Measured but not gated until a NUC run assigns its budget (#2195).

card_list.note: Board card list, default 200-row cap with X-Total-Count/X-Truncated. Page read without a window count; a full page adds one bare COUNT (#2239).

cards_archived.note: First archived-cards page (50 rows). Page read without a window count; a full page adds one bare COUNT on the archived_at index (#2239).

board_movements.note: Board History first page (50 rows, newest first). Page query on the (board, -moved_at) index plus a bare COUNT, no window count (#1961). Measured but not gated until a NUC run assigns its budget (#2237).

board_movements_deep.note: Board History at a deep offset, derived from the first page's count at run time. Measured but not gated until a NUC run assigns its budget (#2237).

board_movements_dated.note: Board History with the date filter, a half-open datetime range on moved_at instead of a __date cast (#1961). Measured but not gated until a NUC run assigns its budget (#2237).

notifications_list.note: The frontend polls this every 15-30s (visiban/settings.py's DEFAULT_THROTTLE_RATES comment) -- the highest-QPS authenticated endpoint in the product, even though its own per-request cost is capped at 50 rows by NotificationListView.

notifications_unread.note: Companion to notifications_list -- polled at the same interval; unlike the list it is uncapped (counts all accessible unread rows).

board_summary.note: Per-swimlane counts plus a replay of the cards that entered a done column in the last 30 days (#448). Before #448 this was SQL aggregates only.

board_analytics.note: Heatmap, stalled cards and blocked time, with a replay of the cards relevant to the default 30-day window plus the frozen avg_days_per_column prefetch (#448).

flow_cycle_time.note: Replays every movement of the fixture board in Python (one query), then samples completions in the default 90-day range (#448).

flow_throughput.note: Same replay as flow_cycle_time, bucketed into whole ISO weeks (#448).

flow_cumulative_flow.note: Same replay; 90 days x columns from a difference array, never a per-day query (#448).

flow_wip_age.note: Same replay plus one query each for block rows and blocking relations (#448).

flow_dwell.note: Same replay as cumulative flow, then completed dwell percentiles per column (#2260).

flow_blocked.note: Same replay plus block rows and blocking relations (#2260).

flow_attention.note: Same replay plus blocking relations and the card directory (#2260).

flow_swimlanes.note: Same replay as cycle time plus block rows, bucketed per swimlane (#2266).

analytics_overview.path: 8 reads, each with ?days=90 as the overview sends: analytics/, metrics/{cycle-time,throughput,cumulative-flow,wip-age,dwell,blocked,attention}/ on the load-test board
analytics_overview.note: The overview open on the active-only board (#2430). The overview's eight reads fired at once (#2426); wall time to the last response, peak RSS of the one server process.

aged_analytics_overview.path: the same 8 reads, each with ?days=90, on the aged board
